summary.one_liner: Keycloak is an open source identity and access management server that adds authentication and user management to applications and services.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Keycloak as providing user federation, strong authentication, user management, and fine-grained authorization. It is meant to let applications add login and secure services without building their own user storage or authentication. To start it, the README says to unzip the downloaded distribution and run bin/kc.sh (or kc.bat) start-dev, or to run the quay.io/keycloak/keycloak Docker image with start-dev. Build instructions, a testing guide, and a contributing guide are linked from the README rather than included. The repository also points to related projects: server and Java adapters, client libraries, QuickStarts, and a Node.js Connect adapter.
use_cases: add login to a web app
how_to_run: Download the Keycloak distribution from the project website and unzip it
notable: Provides user federation, strong authentication, user management, and fine-grained authorization
Can be started with a single start-dev command or a Docker image
Includes Java server and adapters, plus client libraries and a Node.js Connect adapter in related projects
Governed by the CNCF Code of Conduct
caveats: The README covers only quick start; building, testing, and full setup are in external guides
start-dev is a development mode command; the README does not describe production deployment here
